newsitem.title: MEXICO: Leftist killed in south Mexico in bloody week.
newsitem.headline: Leftist killed in south Mexico in bloody week.

text.p: A prominent leftist was shot and killed in southern Mexico, the latest in a string of deaths within the opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), police said on Saturday.
Santana Alonso Arellano was killed on Friday in a village near the border between Guerrero and Michoacan states, a police spokesman in the Guerrero city of Altamirano said.

The Mexico City daily Reforma said Alonso, whose brother is a former Guerrero lawmaker for the PRD, was shot twice in the face while his hands and legs were bound. His death followed that of at least four other members of the PRD in Guerrero in the last week.

On March 22, a former PRD mayor and his wife were shot in front of their grandchildren in the village of Xalpatlahuac. A PRD supporter was shot on Monday in the village of Tuxtepec and on Tuesday a local party leader was run over and killed as he walked out of PRD headquarters in the state capital of Chilpancingo. The car that hit him did not stop.
Also last week, Felix Salgado, a national PRD senator in Guerrero, was run off a main highway as he rode his motorbike, in what he suspected was an attempt on his life.
"There are dark interests that are seeking to wipe out the PRD in Guerrero ... (prior to) the July 6 elections," Reforma quoted him as saying on Saturday after he left the hospital.

Party leaders in Mexico City have sought a meeting with President Ernesto Zedillo to demand a halt to the violence, which has stirred up fears ahead of the July 6 mid-term elections for the lower house of Congress.

Zedillo's party, the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), has ruled Mexico for 68 years but was expected to suffer some heavy setbacks at the ballot box. The PRD blames PRI supporters for much of the violence.
